_readme: NAMED OWNERS FOR WORKFLOWS THAT ARE OFF THE PR PATH (task-dee226be3107a98b c4).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A workflow on the PR path has an owner by construction: the
person whose PR it reddens. Move it to `push: main` and that owner disappears --
it cannot block a merge, no PR ever surfaces it, and a lane's close-out reads its
own PRs, never main's health. posix-vacuous-green-census.yml failed on main's tip
for ELEVEN HOURS across EIGHT consecutive runs and cost nobody a second
(task-6005859f86872319). scripts/main-red-owner.sh answers 'somebody must be told';
this file answers 'WHO'. Without it the watcher's issue is addressed to the repo,
which is the same nobody one layer out.
THE INCIDENT WORKFLOW HAS NO ROW HERE ANY MORE, AND THAT IS THE GUARD WORKING.
posix-vacuous-green-census.yml was put BACK on the PR path on 2026-09-16 after the
same class recurred: 36 consecutive red census runs on main, from 9b9e26c23 onward,
for two freshly-landed unguarded scripts. On the PR path it has an owner by
construction again -- the author of the PR that adds the unguarded script -- so the
derived population no longer contains it, and workflow-owner-check.sh reds on a
STALE row for an on-PR workflow exactly as it reds on a MISSING row for an off-PR
one. It did, which is how this row came out.
AND AGAIN, 2026-09-17: pipefail-sigpipe-scan.yml. Its row said a per-PR run would
re-scan the tree 'to re-derive an unchanged verdict'. The verdict was not unchanged.
Off the PR path it failed on FIFTEEN consecutive pushes to main (50 of its last 100
push runs red) with 'RATCHET BROKEN -- 104 finding(s) at confidence >= high, baseline
is 101': three new sites had landed through PRs that never ran it, and every red
named an author who had not written them. Back on the PR path, so the row is gone and
the guard reds on the stale row -- which is how it came out (task-4f360efc26a428f5).
THE POPULATION IS DERIVED, NEVER CURATED. A workflow belongs here iff it carries a
`push:` arm and NO `pull_request:` arm -- i.e. it is off the PR path, so only the
watcher can see its red. scripts/workflow-owner-check.sh recomputes that set from
the workflow files on every run and REFUSES when it does not match the keys below.
You cannot move a workflow off the PR path and forget this file: the guard reds.
`owner` IS A LANE, not a person. Lanes are the repo's own fence table (CLAUDE.md):
api, console, deploy, gates, cli, studio. A lane outlives any individual and is
the unit a close-out can actually be pointed at. `owner` must be one of those six.
`why_off_pr` IS LOAD-BEARING and is the one line the row demands for every move:
why the PR is the wrong place for this check, in a sentence a reader can dispute.

cli-release-cadence.yml.why_off_pr: asks whether the RELEASE CADENCE has slipped -- a property of the tag history over time, not of any one diff; a PR cannot make it true or false.

cli-release.yml.why_off_pr: publishes a release from a tag; running it on a PR head would cut artifacts from unmerged code.

deploy.yml.why_off_pr: ships merged code to real hosts; a PR head must never reach a box.

grip-suite.yml.why_off_pr: the Grip ledger suite reads durable ledger state, not the diff; on a PR it measures the same thing every time at full cost.

landed-mark.yml.why_off_pr: records that a PR LANDED -- the event it reports does not exist until the merge commit does.

release-artifact.yml.why_off_pr: builds and uploads release artifacts for a pushed ref.

release.yml.why_off_pr: cuts the release itself; tag-shaped, not diff-shaped.

scaffy-catalog-drift.yml.why_off_pr: compares the scaffy catalog against the templates on main; the comparand IS main, so on a PR it answers about the base, not the change.

seal-reading.yml.why_off_pr: seals a reading over landed history; nothing is sealed until the commit is on main.

twoslash.yml.why_off_pr: type-checks docs snippets against the PUBLISHED SDK surface, which only changes on a release.
